findings.what: No screen says the rule that sorts the three cases, r = (−c ± √(c² − 4mk)) ÷ 2m with the sign of c² − 4mk deciding, but a steps lesson shows only its screens; it appears only as screen 3's readout label, and screen 4's Why ('they meet when the square root is of zero') points at a square root no screen has shown, so add that sentence to screen 3, trimming its 'On the left… On the right…' opening to stay under 90 words.

findings.where: screen 6 Why ('Heavier damping') and screen 7 text
findings.what: 'The two roots always multiply to 4. So more damping pushes the fast root away from zero and pulls the slow one in' does not follow from the product alone: the missing step is that the roots also add to −c ÷ m (−5 at damping 5, −6 at damping 6), and no screen says where either fact comes from, which is the factorising of screen 2: they multiply to k ÷ m and add to −c ÷ m.

The sizes 0.667 and −0.167 appear with no working; the screen has room, at about 55 words, for one line saying that starting at 0.5 m at rest gives A + B = 0.5 and −A − 4B = 0, so B = −0.167 and A = 0.667 (checked by hand: correct).

The screen never states its point, that critical is the quickest return that never swings past rest; it ends by naming 'critical damping', so lead with the point and cut the second number sentence to keep it near 80 words.

'The answer then needs a second part, t e^(−2t)' is asserted and no screen shows that it satisfies the rule; one work line would close the gap: x = (0.5 + t)e^(−2t) gives x′ = −2t e^(−2t) and x″ = (4t − 2)e^(−2t), which sum with 4x′ and 4x to 0 (checked by hand).

'Damping 3 crosses rest sooner' has no clear comparison, because the critical trace never crosses rest; say 'Damping 3 reaches rest sooner, at about 1.8 s, but swings past it' (computed: the c = 3 trace first crosses zero at 1.83 s).

α in 'e^(αt)' is never defined on a screen, since α ± jβ appears only in the closing summary; write 'a mirror pair α ± jβ, here −1 ± j1.732'. The reason the shadow is the answer, that the mirror root's arrow turns the other way so the two add to a real number, is only in the explanation text, which a steps lesson does not show.

The worked loop never ties its 980 rad/s, about 156 Hz, to the 1000 rad/s, 159 Hz this same 100 mH and 10 µF pair resonates at, which Dan already knows from AC circuits; hertz never appears on a screen either, even though reading β as hertz is a listed common mistake (all loop numbers checked by hand: 1600 < 40000, −200 ± j979.8, 155.9 Hz, 5 ms, 200 Ω).

The brief's naval tie-in is missing from every screen: ship roll at small angles is this equation, the straight version holds only at small angles, roll damping grows with forward speed, and roll decay is an exponentially decaying cosine; one sentence in screen 11's Why or screen 9 would carry it.

Each SHOW text is about 80 words, within the limit, but the 23-word lead ('A 1 kg mass hangs on a 4 N/m spring…') repeats above it, so Dan reads about 105 words a screen; consider dropping the lead on SHOW screens after screen 1.
'It would never die only with a real part of 0.' reads awkwardly; try 'It would ring for ever only if the real part were 0.'
'c = 6' labels only the left end of the grey real-axis path (−5.24); the other end at −0.76 is also c = 6 and has no label, so the path can read as running from c = 6 to c = 4 in one direction only.
